# RFC-0008: NCU source wire contract

> **Version:** 0.1.0 | **Status:** draft | **Phase:** spec

**References:** [RFC-0001](../rfc/RFC-0001.md), [RFC-0002](../rfc/RFC-0002.md), [RFC-0003](../rfc/RFC-0003.md), [RFC-0004](../rfc/RFC-0004.md), [RFC-0005](../rfc/RFC-0005.md), [RFC-0002:C-DEFAULT-MACHINE-OUTPUT](../rfc/RFC-0002.md#rfc-0002c-default-machine-output), [RFC-0002:C-SUCCESS-RESPONSE](../rfc/RFC-0002.md#rfc-0002c-success-response), [RFC-0002:C-ERROR-RESPONSE](../rfc/RFC-0002.md#rfc-0002c-error-response), [RFC-0002:C-STDOUT-STDERR](../rfc/RFC-0002.md#rfc-0002c-stdout-stderr), [RFC-0002:C-FORMAT-PROJECTIONS](../rfc/RFC-0002.md#rfc-0002c-format-projections), [RFC-0003:C-ROW-KEY](../rfc/RFC-0003.md#rfc-0003c-row-key), [RFC-0004:C-SOURCE-IDENTITY](../rfc/RFC-0004.md#rfc-0004c-source-identity), [RFC-0004:C-SOURCE-VERSION](../rfc/RFC-0004.md#rfc-0004c-source-version), [RFC-0004:C-TRACE-DETECTION](../rfc/RFC-0004.md#rfc-0004c-trace-detection), [RFC-0004:C-COMMAND-SURFACE](../rfc/RFC-0004.md#rfc-0004c-command-surface), [RFC-0005:C-ARTIFACT-ROOT](../rfc/RFC-0005.md#rfc-0005c-artifact-root), [RFC-0005:C-FRESHNESS](../rfc/RFC-0005.md#rfc-0005c-freshness)

---

## 1. Summary

### [RFC-0008:C-SUMMARY] Summary (Informative) <a id="rfc-0008c-summary"></a>

This RFC specifies the Nsight Compute source wire contract for VeloQ.
It refines the product, CLI I/O, list identity, source, and artifact contracts in [RFC-0001](../rfc/RFC-0001.md), [RFC-0002](../rfc/RFC-0002.md), [RFC-0003](../rfc/RFC-0003.md), [RFC-0004](../rfc/RFC-0004.md), and [RFC-0005](../rfc/RFC-0005.md) for the NCU source.

**Scope:** This RFC covers the stable NCU source identity, supported input form, source-owned command IDs, NCU launch row identifiers, concrete NCU row key formats, metric enum-name fields, generated artifacts, source-specific output exceptions, and compatibility rules for source version `v1`. It does not prescribe private helper script implementation, Python discovery internals, private cache lock mechanics, raw `ncu_report` object layout, disassembly pipeline internals, or full response field inventories beyond the invariants named here; full response field inventories are exposed by the NCU `schema` targets.

**Rationale:** NCU is a shipped VeloQ source with a stable `v1` source version. Agents need source-specific launch identity, metric enum semantics, and cache behavior documented so they can compare kernel reports and drill into launches without reverse-engineering the native sidecar implementation.

---

## 2. Specification

### [RFC-0008:C-SOURCE-IDENTITY] Source identity (Normative) <a id="rfc-0008c-source-identity"></a>

NCU success responses MUST set `source.kind` to `ncu`.

NCU success responses MUST set `source.version` to `v1` for the wire contract specified by this RFC.

NCU handled error responses MUST set `source.kind` to `ncu` when source context is known.

NCU handled error responses MUST set `source.version` to `v1` when source context is known.

The NCU source namespace MUST be `ncu`.

An NCU source-owned command ID MUST use the `ncu.<verb>` form.

An NCU trace-bearing success response MUST include `trace` when the input path is known.

An NCU trace-bearing handled error response MUST include `trace` when the input path is known.

NCU responses SHOULD omit `trace_span` because NCU reports do not expose a single trace-wide wall-clock time span comparable to NSys timeline traces.

The NCU `schema` command MUST NOT require a trace input.

The NCU `schema` command MUST omit `trace` and `trace_span` from its envelope.

A breaking change to an NCU source payload MUST change the NCU source version according to [RFC-0004:C-SOURCE-VERSION](../rfc/RFC-0004.md#rfc-0004c-source-version).

**Rationale:** Source identity, source version, and command IDs are the dispatch context agents use after parsing an envelope. NCU has a distinct report model from timeline traces, so omitting `trace_span` is a source-specific semantic choice, not missing metadata.

### [RFC-0008:C-SUPPORTED-INPUTS] Supported inputs (Normative) <a id="rfc-0008c-supported-inputs"></a>

NCU automatic source detection MUST follow the side-effect-free trace detection contract in [RFC-0004:C-TRACE-DETECTION](../rfc/RFC-0004.md#rfc-0004c-trace-detection).

NCU automatic source detection MUST claim path names whose extension is `.ncu-rep`.

NCU automatic source detection MUST NOT claim `.nsys-rep`, `_pqtdir`, `.pt.trace.json`, `.pt.trace.json.gz`, `.sqlite`, or path names whose extension is not `.ncu-rep`.

An NCU trace-bearing command MUST accept `.ncu-rep` report inputs when the report is present and a fresh or buildable native sidecar is available.

An NCU trace-bearing command MAY accept a missing `.ncu-rep` report path when the corresponding VeloQ artifact root already contains a readable native NCU sidecar with a supported native schema.

An NCU trace-bearing command MUST emit a handled diagnostic error when neither the `.ncu-rep` report nor a readable native NCU sidecar with a supported native schema is available.

An NCU command that opens a supported input MUST keep generated artifacts under the artifact root defined by [RFC-0005:C-ARTIFACT-ROOT](../rfc/RFC-0005.md#rfc-0005c-artifact-root).

**Rationale:** Detection must remain deterministic and side-effect-free. Committed-sidecar mode lets tests, examples, and leak-free artifacts query a report-shaped path without shipping proprietary `.ncu-rep` files that may contain local machine details.

### [RFC-0008:C-COMMAND-SURFACE] Command surface (Normative) <a id="rfc-0008c-command-surface"></a>

The stable NCU source-owned command surface MUST include `summary`, `launches`, `inspect`, `metrics`, `disasm`, `ranges`, `graphs`, `sources`, `source-metrics`, `warp-stalls`, and `schema`.

The stable NCU source-owned command surface MUST preserve the source command rules in [RFC-0004:C-COMMAND-SURFACE](../rfc/RFC-0004.md#rfc-0004c-command-surface).

The NCU `schema` command MUST emit a normal VeloQ JSON envelope.

The NCU `schema` command envelope `data` field MUST be an object with `target` and `schema` fields.

The NCU `schema` command envelope `data.target` field MUST equal the requested schema target string.

The NCU `schema` command envelope `data.schema` field MUST contain the requested JSON schema document.

The NCU `schema` command MUST omit `trace` because it does not inspect a report.

The NCU `schema` command target set MUST include `summary`, `launches`, `inspect`, `metrics`, `disasm`, `ranges`, `graphs`, `sources`, `source-metrics`, and `warp-stalls`.

The NCU `schema` command targets SHOULD be treated as the complete response field inventory for their corresponding NCU payloads.

A gated hidden or unstable NCU command or schema target MUST NOT be treated as part of the stable public command surface until this clause explicitly lists it as stable.

A command added to the stable NCU public command surface MUST either conform to [RFC-0002](../rfc/RFC-0002.md), [RFC-0003](../rfc/RFC-0003.md), [RFC-0004](../rfc/RFC-0004.md), and this RFC, or document a source-specific exception in this RFC.

NCU JSON-mode successes and handled diagnostics MUST use normal VeloQ envelopes.

NCU CSV and table projections MUST follow [RFC-0002:C-FORMAT-PROJECTIONS](../rfc/RFC-0002.md#rfc-0002c-format-projections).

NCU source-owned commands MUST NOT write progress output to stdout in JSON mode.

NCU source-owned commands MUST NOT define a raw-stdout success exception unless this RFC is amended to list that exception.

**Rationale:** The command surface is part of the external agent contract. NCU currently has no raw-stdout exception; every machine-readable success and handled failure should remain envelope-shaped.

### [RFC-0008:C-ROW-ID] Launch row identifiers (Normative) <a id="rfc-0008c-row-id"></a>

An NCU launch identifier exposed as `row_id` MUST use the `launch:<idx>` string form.

The `<idx>` component MUST be a base-10 non-negative integer string.

An NCU `launch:<idx>` row identifier MUST refer to the zero-based launch position in the native launch list for the opened report.

An NCU `launches.rows[]` row `key` MUST equal its `row_id`.

An NCU `launches.rows[]` row `row_id` MUST be accepted by NCU `inspect`.

An NCU `inspect` request for an out-of-range `launch:<idx>` row identifier MUST return a success response.

An NCU `inspect` response for an out-of-range launch row identifier MUST include a row tagged with `type: "not_found"`.

An NCU `inspect` not-found row MUST carry `key` equal to the requested row identifier.

An NCU `inspect` not-found row MUST carry `row_id` equal to the requested row identifier.

NCU drill commands other than `inspect` MAY reject malformed, unsupported-kind, or out-of-range launch row identifiers with handled diagnostic errors.

An NCU launch row identifier MUST NOT expose a packed binary key in place of the human-readable `launch:<idx>` form.

**Rationale:** Agents commonly take `ncu launches` rows and pass their `row_id` to `inspect`, `disasm`, `source-metrics`, or `warp-stalls`. A readable launch identifier keeps drill workflows simple while allowing strict errors for verbs that cannot produce partial batches.

### [RFC-0008:C-ROW-KEYS] Concrete row keys (Normative) <a id="rfc-0008c-row-keys"></a>

NCU row keys MUST follow the canonical list identity contract in [RFC-0003:C-ROW-KEY](../rfc/RFC-0003.md#rfc-0003c-row-key).

NCU row keys MUST be treated by consumers as opaque equality strings.

Consumers SHOULD NOT parse NCU row keys by splitting on delimiter characters because trace-derived names and file paths may contain those characters.

`ncu summary` rows MUST use `totals` for the single summary row key.

`ncu launches` rows MUST use `launch:<idx>` for both `key` and `row_id`.

`ncu inspect` found launch rows MUST use `launch:<idx>` for both `key` and `row_id`.

`ncu inspect` not-found rows MUST use the requested row identifier for both `key` and `row_id`.

`ncu metrics` long-form rows MUST use `launch:<idx>|counter:<name>`.

`ncu metrics` per-launch rows MUST use `launch:<idx>`.

`ncu disasm` kernel rows MUST use `kernel|<function_name>`.

`ncu ranges` rows MUST use `range:<idx>`.

`ncu graphs` rows MUST use `graph:<idx>`.

`ncu sources` rows MUST use `source:<launch_idx>`.

`ncu source-metrics --by line` rows MUST use `launch:<idx>|line:<file>:<line>`.

`ncu source-metrics --by sass` rows MUST use `launch:<idx>|sass:0x<addr>` with a lowercase hexadecimal address and no leading zero padding requirement.

`ncu source-metrics --by file` rows MUST use `launch:<idx>|file:<file>`.

`ncu warp-stalls --by line` rows MUST use `launch:<idx>|line:<file>:<line>`.

`ncu warp-stalls --by sass` rows MUST use `launch:<idx>|sass:0x<addr>` with a lowercase hexadecimal address and no leading zero padding requirement.

`ncu warp-stalls --by reason` rows MUST use `launch:<idx>|reason:<reason>`.

A stable NCU response that adds a new primary `rows[]` item shape MUST define that shape's row key in this clause before it is treated as part of the stable public contract.

**Rationale:** Row keys are the join substrate for agent workflows and cross-report comparison. The key formats must be stable enough to compare equal rows, while consumers must avoid delimiter parsing because NCU names and source paths are trace data rather than schema tokens.

### [RFC-0008:C-METRIC-ENUMS] Metric enum fields (Normative) <a id="rfc-0008c-metric-enums"></a>

NCU metric payloads that expose metric type information MUST report `metric_type` as a stable enum-name string.

NCU metric payloads that expose metric subtype information MUST report `metric_subtype` as a stable enum-name string when the subtype is known.

NCU metric payloads that expose rollup information MUST report `rollup` as a stable enum-name string when the rollup is known.

NCU metric payloads MAY omit `metric_subtype` or `rollup` when the native report has no corresponding value.

NCU metric payloads SHOULD preserve native integer enum codes as `metric_type_code`, `metric_subtype_code`, and `rollup_code` when those codes are available.

NCU metric enum-name fields MUST use `unknown` rather than failing deserialization when a future NCU version exposes a value VeloQ does not yet name.

NCU metric enum-name fields MUST NOT be replaced by integer-only fields without an NCU source version bump.

NCU metric enum code fields MUST remain auxiliary to the enum-name fields.

**Rationale:** Agents need readable, stable metric categories for jq filters and reports. Keeping native integer codes alongside names preserves diagnostic detail without making consumers depend on NVIDIA's raw enum numbering.

### [RFC-0008:C-ARTIFACTS] Artifacts and caches (Normative) <a id="rfc-0008c-artifacts"></a>

NCU generated artifacts MUST live under the report artifact root defined by [RFC-0005:C-ARTIFACT-ROOT](../rfc/RFC-0005.md#rfc-0005c-artifact-root).

NCU's native report sidecar MUST be named `ncu-native.json.gz` within the report artifact root.

NCU's native sidecar freshness marker MUST be named `ncu-native.sha256` within the report artifact root.

NCU MAY create an `ncu-native.lock` file within the report artifact root while coordinating native sidecar builds.

NCU commands MAY leave `ncu-native.lock` in the artifact root after command completion.

NCU disassembly correlation artifacts MUST live under `disasm/` within the report artifact root.

NCU disassembly correlation JSON artifacts MUST use the `disasm/<sha>.correlated.json` path form within the report artifact root.

NCU extracted cubin artifacts MAY use the `disasm/<sha>.cubin` path form within the report artifact root.

When the `.ncu-rep` report exists, NCU native sidecar freshness MUST be keyed on a content hash of the report bytes rather than on local absolute paths.

When the `.ncu-rep` report is missing but a readable native sidecar with a supported native schema exists, NCU MAY treat that sidecar as authoritative committed-sidecar input.

NCU command-line query workflows MUST accept the report path as the user-facing input.

NCU command-line query workflows MUST NOT require users to pass `ncu-native.json.gz`, `ncu-native.sha256`, `ncu-native.lock`, or `disasm/` child paths as positional inputs.

A stale or missing NCU native sidecar MUST be reported as a handled diagnostic when VeloQ cannot rebuild it from the report.

This RFC specifies source-owned artifact names and ownership, not the private lock acquisition or removal algorithm.

**Rationale:** NCU artifacts need checkout-stable freshness and leak-free committed fixtures. Keeping all artifacts under the report root lets `veloq clean` and agent workflows reason about ownership without knowing implementation details.

### [RFC-0008:C-SOURCE-EXCEPTIONS] Source-specific output exceptions (Normative) <a id="rfc-0008c-source-exceptions"></a>

NCU has no stable raw-stdout success exception.

NCU JSON-mode successes MUST write exactly one VeloQ success envelope to stdout.

NCU JSON-mode handled failures MUST write exactly one VeloQ error envelope to stdout.

NCU CSV and table successes MUST replace the JSON envelope on stdout according to [RFC-0002:C-FORMAT-PROJECTIONS](../rfc/RFC-0002.md#rfc-0002c-format-projections).

NCU CSV and table handled failures MAY write a human-readable mirror to stderr according to [RFC-0002:C-STDOUT-STDERR](../rfc/RFC-0002.md#rfc-0002c-stdout-stderr).

NCU progress output MUST NOT be written to stdout in JSON mode.

NCU `schema` successes MUST remain JSON-envelope responses and MUST NOT be treated as raw schema stdout.

NCU's omission of `trace_span` MUST be treated as a source-specific trace model rule rather than as an output exception.

**Rationale:** Agents can safely parse stdout when every JSON-mode NCU result is envelope-shaped. The only projection exception is the source-neutral CSV/table rule already defined by the CLI I/O contract.

### [RFC-0008:C-COMPATIBILITY] Compatibility (Normative) <a id="rfc-0008c-compatibility"></a>

Adding optional NCU response fields MAY remain compatible with source version `v1` when existing field meanings, row identifiers, row keys, command IDs, and error envelope semantics are preserved.

Adding a new stable NCU command or stable schema target MAY remain compatible with source version `v1` when it conforms to this RFC and the source contracts it references.

Changing `source.kind`, the `ncu` namespace, or the `ncu.<verb>` command ID form MUST be treated as breaking.

Removing or renaming a command listed in [RFC-0008:C-COMMAND-SURFACE](../rfc/RFC-0008.md#rfc-0008c-command-surface) MUST be treated as breaking.

Changing `launch:<idx>` row identifier syntax or the zero-based native launch position meaning MUST be treated as breaking.

Changing a row key format listed in [RFC-0008:C-ROW-KEYS](../rfc/RFC-0008.md#rfc-0008c-row-keys) MUST be treated as breaking unless the change is limited to a row shape that was explicitly unstable.

Changing NCU metric enum-name fields to integer-only fields MUST be treated as breaking.

Changing the relationship between metric enum-name fields and their auxiliary raw code fields MUST be treated as breaking.

Changing supported input detection so NCU no longer claims `.ncu-rep` paths MUST be treated as breaking.

Changing NCU artifact ownership so generated NCU artifacts leave the report artifact root MUST be treated as breaking.

Changing JSON-mode NCU successes or handled failures away from the VeloQ envelope contract MUST be treated as breaking.

Changing the NCU `trace_span` policy from omitted to populated MAY remain compatible only when the added field follows [RFC-0002](../rfc/RFC-0002.md) envelope extension rules and does not change existing field meanings.

**Rationale:** The NCU source is already `v1`. Compatibility needs to distinguish additive schema growth from changes that would break agent dispatch, row joins, drill commands, metric filters, or cache ownership assumptions.
